graph.summary: Mycophenolate Mofetil → Mycophenolic acid → Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 2 → GMP biosynthetic process → lymphocyte proliferation → Lupus Nephritis

evidence.snippet: Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is the ester prodrug of the immunosuppressant agent mycophenolic acid (MPA) and is rapidly activated by esterases after oral administration.
evidence.explanation: Confirms MMF is a prodrug of MPA, hydrolyzed by esterases to release the active metabolite MPA.

paper.title: Involvement of carboxylesterase 1 and 2 in the hydrolysis of mycophenolate mofetil.
paper.journal: Drug metabolism and disposition: the biological fate of chemicals

evidence.snippet: Mycophenolic acid (MPA) is a potent, selective, noncompetitive and reversible inhibitor of inosine-5'-monophosphate deshydrogenase (IMPDH).
evidence.explanation: MPA directly and selectively inhibits IMPDH2, decreasing its enzymatic activity.

evidence.snippet: MPA effectively inhibited IMPDH activity in a dose-dependent manner, with 94-96% inhibition at concentrations of 100 μM and above.
evidence.explanation: In vitro demonstration of MPA dose-dependently inhibiting IMPDH activity, supporting decreases activity of edge.

paper.title: Combination Effects of Aminolevulinic Acid and Mycophenolic Acid on Hacat Cell Proliferation and Inhibition of Inosine Monophosphate Dehydrogenase.

evidence.snippet: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) is the critical, rate-limiting enzyme in the de novo biosynthesis pathway for guanine nucleotides.
evidence.explanation: IMPDH is the rate-limiting enzyme for de novo guanine nucleotide (GMP) biosynthesis; its activity positively regulates the GMP biosynthetic process.

paper.title: Targeted disruption of the inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase type I gene in mice.

evidence.snippet: Mycophenolic acid (MPA) blocks the key enzyme inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase and the production of guanosine nucleotides required for DNA synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Blocking IMPDH prevents guanosine nucleotide production, confirming IMPDH positively regulates GMP biosynthesis.

paper.title: Mycophenolic acid formulations in adult renal transplantation - update on efficacy and tolerability.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism of action of mycophenolic acid (MPA) has been described as a blockade of inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) and is thought to selectively influence T- and B-lymphocytes due to their strong dependency on guanine nucleotides synthesized via the de novo purine synthesis pathway.
evidence.explanation: T and B lymphocytes depend on the de novo guanine nucleotide synthesis pathway for proliferation; GMP biosynthesis positively regulates lymphocyte proliferation.

paper.title: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase inhibition by mycophenolic acid impairs maturation and function of dendritic cells.
paper.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

evidence.snippet: The description more than 30 years ago of the role of de novo purine synthesis in T and B lymphocytes clonal proliferation opened the possibility for selective immunosuppression by targeting specific enzymatic pathways.
evidence.explanation: De novo purine (guanosine) synthesis is required for T and B lymphocyte clonal proliferation, supporting that GMP biosynthesis positively regulates lymphocyte proliferation.

paper.title: Mycophenolic acid formulations in adult renal transplantation - update on efficacy and tolerability.

evidence.snippet: The thorough inhibition of B cell activation and plasma cell formation by MMF might explain the favorable outcomes of previous clinical trials in patients with SLE, since enhanced B cell proliferation is a hallmark of this disease.
evidence.explanation: Enhanced B cell proliferation is a hallmark of SLE/lupus nephritis; inhibiting it with MMF leads to favorable clinical outcomes, confirming lymphocyte proliferation contributes to lupus nephritis.

paper.title: Mycophenolic acid counteracts B cell proliferation and plasmablast formation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.

evidence.snippet: The most prevalent severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus is nephritis, which is characterized by immune complex deposition, inflammation, and scarring in glomeruli and the tubulointerstitium.
evidence.explanation: Lupus nephritis is the most prevalent severe manifestation of SLE, driven by immune complex deposition from dysregulated lymphocyte activity.

paper.title: In situ B cell-mediated immune responses and tubulointerstitial inflammation in human lupus nephritis.
